summary: The single checkpoint-free H200 discriminator passed: local KV heads 16->8 conservatively saved 0.032131703 seconds/request versus 0.018165159 required, with grouped page-1 FP8 attention, finite consumed outputs, zero live/peak allocation delta, and no dense/repeated KV cache.

provider_spend_basis: Conservative full-project charge: measured bench exposure from registration at 2026-07-19T12:21:48.717260Z through final ready release at 2026-07-19T12:46:47.504712Z was 1498.787452 seconds, or $1.024171 at the bound $2.46/H200-hour rate; rounded upward to $1.03 to cover the separately unmetered 100-GiB disk while the invoice is pending.
causal_interpretation: Measured: halving local KV heads reduced the paired fused-QKV plus write plus attention boundary by 27.33% at the median. The paged-attention median fell 33.92% and supplied about 90% of median total saving, despite effective read bandwidth falling from 1384 to 1047 GB/s. The fused-QKV median fell only 11.51% although output width fell 25%; this is consistent with the candidate's analytical 96-block/72.7%-of-one-H200-wave geometry versus the baseline's 128-block/97.0% wave. Inferred: reduced compulsory FP8 cache traffic dominates, while SM underfill limits the linear benefit.
